security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU's get_physical_address() PTW loop, if the Svnapot N-bit check (PTE_N at cpu_helper.c:1449) or the NAPOT decode logic (cpu_helper.c:1645) is inadvertently gated on first_stage==true, G-stage PTEs with the N bit set would either be incorrectly rejected as reserved (denial_of_service) or silently treated as non-NAPOT entries, computing wrong physical addresses. Additionally, if ext_svnapot==true but the G-stage hgatp-configured levels/vm differ from VS-stage satp, the leaf-PTE napot_bits validation (i != levels-1, napot_bits != 4) could trigger spurious TRANSLATE_FAIL on valid hypervisor G-stage NAPOT superpages, causing unexpected G-stage page faults injected into the guest.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: search for any 'first_stage' boolean condition used as a guard around ext_svnapot, PTE_N, napot_bits, or napot_mask computation in target/riscv/cpu_helper.c get_physical_address(); also search for missing HENVCFG or hgatp-dependent gating that would prevent NAPOT decode in the two_stage && !first_stage G-stage walk path
security_spec.summary: QEMU must ensure ext_svnapot and PTE_N decode apply uniformly to both first_stage (VS-stage) and second_stage (G-stage/hgatp) page table walks; any first_stage gate on NAPOT handling would corrupt G-stage physical address computation and break hypervisor memory isolation

findings.finding: Svnapot N-bit reservation check at line 1449 is NOT gated on first_stage. It reads 'if (!riscv_cpu_cfg(env)->ext_svnapot && (pte & PTE_N))' — this guard applies uniformly to both VS-stage and G-stage PTEs. When ext_svnapot is enabled, G-stage PTEs with the N bit set will pass through to the leaf decode logic correctly. No denial-of-service risk: the first_stage variable is not used as a guard here.

NAPT decode logic at line 1645 is NOT gated on first_stage. It reads 'if (riscv_cpu_cfg(env)->ext_svnapot && (pte & PTE_N))' — this applies uniformly to both stages. When G-stage encounters a leaf PTE with N=1, napot_bits is correctly computed from ppn via ctzl(ppn)+1, and the NAPOT physical address reconstruction at line 1653 uses the computed napot_mask. No first_stage guard prevents G-stage NAPOT processing.

G-stage hgatp level/mode handling is correctly scoped. At lines 1287-1315, when first_stage==false (G-stage), the base/levels/ptidxbits/ptesize are derived from env->hgatp (lines 1306-1314), while VS-stage uses env->satp/env->vsatp (lines 1287-1304). The NAPOT validation at line 1647 '(i != (levels - 1))' correctly uses the G-stage-specific levels when walking G-stage tables. G-stage NAPOT superpages with valid hgatp-configured levels will not trigger spurious TRANSLATE_FAIL due to level mismatch.

HENVCFG gating at lines 1364-1366 applies only to PBMTE and ADUE (pbmte and adue booleans), not to Svnapot. This is correct per the RISC-V privileged spec: Svnapot is a CPU ISA extension (ext_svnapot), not a menvcfg/henvcfg-controlled feature. No HENVCFG bit exists for NAPOT control, so there is no missing HENVCFG gating. The ext_svnapot CPU config flag alone correctly governs both stages.

The PTW loop at line 1378 'for (i = 0; i < levels; i++, ptshift -= ptidxbits)' is stage-agnostic. Variable 'i' and 'levels' are correctly partitioned: when first_stage==false, levels is from hgatp (e.g. Sv39x4=3 levels, Sv48x4=4 levels). The loop walks exactly the G-stage page table depth. There is no cross-contamination between VS-stage and G-stage level counters.
